        "contents": "- Device list CRUD behavior remains exactly as today (no ACL payload sync calls).\n\n### 4.2 Add device sequence (when enabled)\n\n1. User opens Add Device.\n2. UI shows ACL toggles with defaults &#96;current=true&#96;, &#96;history=false&#96;.\n3. On save, add to &#96;KnownDeviceStore&#96;, then sync full list.\n4. If final sync failure occurs, rollback to pre-add snapshot and show a localized error explaining restoration.\n\n### 4.3 Edit device sequence (when enabled)\n\n1. User edits toggles.\n2. Save mutates &#96;KnownDevice&#96;.\n3. Full-list sync is triggered.\n4. If final sync failure occurs, rollback edited values to previous snapshot and notify user.\n\n### 4.4 Remove device sequence (when enabled)\n\n1. User deletes device.\n2. Remove locally.\n3. Re-send full list without removed device.\n4. If final sync failure occurs, restore removed device + previous ACLs/order and notify user.\n\n---\n\n## 5) Unknown visitors section design (Devices screen)\n\n- Data source:\n  - &#96;VisitorHistoryViewModel.sortedVisitors&#96;\n  - filter unique DeviceIDs not in known devices and not in ignored store.\n- UI:\n  - New section above known devices.\n  - Each row shows DeviceID, last seen timestamp, optional location snippet similar to visitor history row style.\n- Actions:\n  - **Allow**: open add-device sheet with prefilled ID + ACL controls.\n  - **Ignore**: persist to ignored list and remove from this section immediately.\n- Visibility:\n  - Section hidden if resulting list is empty.\n\n---\n\n## 6) Copy/texts and privacy communication\n\nThe feature text should explicitly explain:\n\n- It is optional.\n- It requires DeviceKey to protect ACL updates.\n- Once enabled, the app will actively manage and sync who may access current location and history.\n- It cannot be disabled later, but per-device rights remain editable.\n\nSuggested short onboarding title/body:\n\n- **Title**: “Control which devices can access your location data”\n- **Body**: “Optionally enable access control for linked devices. You can define per device whether current location and location history are shared. Parameter serverURL: The server URL to fetch visitor history from\n    private func refreshVisitorHistory(serverURL: URL) async {\n        let currentDeviceID = thisDeviceIDManager.shared.deviceID\n        \n        do {\n            debugLog(\"[DeviceLocationRefresher] refreshVisitorHistory for device \\(currentDeviceID)\")\n            // Request a reasonable amount of visitor history entries (enough to cover 90 seconds)\n            // Assuming updates happen every few seconds, requesting 50 entries should be sufficient\n            APIRequestCounter.shared.record(.getVisitorHistory)\n            let visitors = try await MiataruAPIClient.getVisitorHistory(\n                serverURL: serverURL,\n                forDeviceID: currentDeviceID,\n                deviceKey: settings.deviceKey,\n                amount: 50\n            )\n            \n            // Calculate cutoff time: 90 seconds ago\n            let cutoffTime = Date().addingTimeInterval(-90)\n            \n            // Filter visitors from the past 90 seconds and get unique device IDs\n            let recentVisitorDeviceIDs = Set(visitors\n                .filter { $0.TimeStampDate &gt;= cutoffTime }\n                .map { $0.DeviceID })\n            \n            // Update cache on main thread\n            await MainActor.run {\n                cache.setRecentVisitorDeviceIDs(recentVisitorDeviceIDs)\n            }\n            \n            debugLog(\"[DeviceLocationRefresher] Found \\(recentVisitorDeviceIDs.count) devices that looked for current user in past 90 seconds\")\n        } catch {\n            _ = DeviceKeyAuthHandler.handle(error: error)",

        "contents": "---\nname: VisitorHistoryAutoRefresh\noverview: Align the QR-code tab visitor history refresh behavior with the Devices tab by adding the same visibility-aware, throttled auto-refresh triggers.\ntodos:\n  - id: add-visitor-refresh-throttle\n    content: Add refreshIfNeeded throttling to VisitorHistoryViewModel\n    status: completed\n  - id: wire-qr-view-auto-refresh\n    content: Hook QR view to notifications and visibility\n    status: completed\n  - id: verify-behavior\n    content: Check refreshable + initial load behavior\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n# Visitor History Auto-Refresh Plan\n\n## Current behavior recap\n\n- Devices tab (&#96;/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/iPhone_DevicesView.swift&#96;) triggers refresh on pull-to-refresh plus notifications for own-location updates and app activation, with throttling and visibility checks handled by &#96;DeviceLocationRefresher&#96;.\n- QR-code tab visitor history (&#96;/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView.swift&#96;) only loads on first appear and on manual refresh; it does not auto-refresh while visible.\n- Visitor history data loading lives in &#96;VisitorHistoryViewModel&#96; within &#96;/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/iPhone_VisitorHistoryView.swift&#96;.\n\n## Plan\n\n1. **Add a throttled auto-refresh helper for visitor history**\n\n- Extend &#96;VisitorHistoryViewModel&#96; with a &#96;lastRefresh&#96; timestamp and a &#96;refreshIfNeeded(isVisible:force:)&#96; method similar to &#96;DeviceLocationRefresher.shouldRefresh&#96;, using:\n  - &#96;SettingsManager.shared.autoRefreshDeviceList&#96; as the enable flag.\n  - &#96;SettingsManager.shared.mapUpdateInterval&#96; as the throttle interval.\n  - &#96;UIApplication.shared.applicationState == .active&#96; on main thread to avoid background refresh.\n- Keep &#96;loadVisitorHistory()&#96; as the core fetch, and make &#96;refreshIfNeeded&#96; call it when conditions are met.\n\n1. **Wire QR-code tab to auto-refresh while visible**\n\n- In &#96;iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView&#96;, add a &#96;@State private var isVisible&#96; flag set in &#96;.onAppear&#96; / &#96;.onDisappear&#96;.\n- Add &#96;.onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .didSendOwnLocationUpdate))&#96; to call &#96;visitorHistoryViewModel.refreshIfNeeded(isVisible: isVisible)&#96;.",

        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "struct VisitorHistoryStateView&lt;Content: View&gt;: View {\n    @ObservedObject var viewModel: VisitorHistoryViewModel\n    let content: ([MiataruVisitor]) -&gt; Content\n    \n    var body: some View {\n        if viewModel.isLoading {\n            HStack {\n                Spacer()\n                ProgressView()\n                Spacer()\n            }\n            .padding()\n        } else if let error = viewModel.errorMessage {\n            VStack(spacing: 16) {\n                Text(error)\n                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)\n                    .multilineTextAlignment(.center)\n                Button(NSLocalizedString(\"visitor_history_retry\", comment: \"Button to retry loading visitor history\")) {\n                    Task {\n                        await viewModel.loadVisitorHistory()\n                    }\n                }\n                .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)\n            }\n            .padding()\n            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)\n        } else if viewModel.visitors.isEmpty {\n            VStack(spacing: 8) {\n                Text(NSLocalizedString(\"visitor_history_empty\", comment: \"Empty state message when no visitors have accessed the device\"))\n                    .foregroundColor(.secondary)\n            }\n            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)\n            .padding()\n        } else {\n            content(viewModel.sortedVisitors)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstruct VisitorHistorySection: View {\n    @ObservedObject var viewModel: VisitorHistoryViewModel",

        "contents": "    ///   - amount: The maximum number of visitor history entries to retrieve.\n    /// - Returns: An array of visitor data objects.\n    /// - Throws: An &#96;APIError&#96; if the request fails.\n    public static func getVisitorHistory(serverURL: URL,\n                                  forDeviceID deviceID: String,\n                                  deviceKey: String? = nil,\n                                  amount: Int) async throws -&gt; [MiataruVisitor] {\n        let url = serverURL.appendingPathComponent(\"v1/GetVisitorHistory\")\n\n        let requestBody = GetVisitorHistoryRequestBody(\n            MiataruGetVisitorHistory: GetVisitorHistoryPayload(Device: deviceID, Amount: String(amount), DeviceKey: deviceKey)\n        )\n\n        let data: Data\n        do {\n            data = try await performPostRequest(url: url, encodablePayload: requestBody) {\n                \"[MiataruAPIClient] Requesting visitor history for device \\(deviceID) amount=\\(amount) payload=\\($0)\"\n            }\n        } catch APIError.encodingError(let err) {\n            debugLog(\"[MiataruAPIClient] Encoding visitor history request failed for device \\(deviceID): \\(err.localizedDescription)\")\n            throw APIError.encodingError(err)\n        }\n\n        do {\n            let response = try jsonDecoder.decode(MiataruGetVisitorHistoryResponse.self, from: data)\n            debugLog(\"[MiataruAPIClient] Received visitor history entries=\\(response.MiataruVisitors.count) for device \\(deviceID)\")\n            return response.MiataruVisitors\n        } catch {\n            if let jsonString = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8) {\n                debugLog(\"[MiataruAPIClient] Visitor history decode failed for device \\(deviceID).         "contents": "---\nname: visitor-log-inline\noverview: Move the visitor history from a separate navigation view into an inline section that renders directly under the QR code tab content, reusing the existing visitor history row UI and data loading logic.\ntodos:\n  - id: extract-visitor-section\n    content: Create reusable visitor history section + shared load logic\n    status: completed\n  - id: embed-qr-tab\n    content: Insert inline visitor section below QR code tab content\n    status: completed\n  - id: wire-standalone-view\n    content: Rewire standalone visitor view to reuse shared section\n    status: completed\n  - id: docs-changelog\n    content: Update changelog and relevant docs\n    status: completed\nisProject: false\n---\n\n- Refactor visitor history UI into a reusable inline section view (ex: &#96;VisitorHistorySection&#96;) that renders loading/error/empty/list states using &#96;VisitorHistoryRow&#96; and existing load logic. Keep strings in English-only keys already used.\n- Update &#96;[miataru/views/iPhone/iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView.swift)&#96; to remove the visitor history button/navigation destination and insert the new section below the device ID/share area inside the existing &#96;ScrollView&#96;.\n- Adjust &#96;[miataru/views/iPhone/iPhone_VisitorHistoryView.swift](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/miataru/views/iPhone/iPhone_VisitorHistoryView.swift)&#96; to use the shared inline section content (or shared view model) so the standalone view still works if used elsewhere, without duplicating logic.\n- Verify the layout works in portrait/landscape and that pull-to-refresh still operates in the QR tab (if retained) or provide a retry button when errors occur.\n- Update &#96;[CHANGELOG.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/CHANGELOG.md)&#96; and any relevant docs (for example &#96;[APP_STORE_DESCRIPTION.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/APP_STORE_DESCRIPTION.md)&#96; or &#96;[APP_FEATURES.md](/Users/bietiekay/code/miataru-ios-app/miataru/APP_FEATURES.md)&#96;) to reflect the new inline visitor log placement.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "public struct MiataruVisitor: Codable {\n    public let DeviceID: String\n    public let TimeStamp: String\n\n    /// Computed property for accessing the timestamp as a Date.\n    /// The timestamp from the API is in milliseconds, so we divide by 1000.\n    public var TimeStampDate: Date {\n        if let ts = Double(TimeStamp) {\n            // Timestamps from the API are in milliseconds, convert to seconds\n            return Date(timeIntervalSince1970: ts / 1000.0)\n        } else {\n            return Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 0)\n        }\n    }\n    \n    /// Unique identifier combining DeviceID and TimeStamp for use in ForEach\n    public var uniqueID: String {\n        return \"\\(DeviceID)-\\(TimeStamp)\"\n    }\n\n    enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {\n        case DeviceID\n        case TimeStamp\n    }\n\n    public init(DeviceID: String, TimeStamp: String) {\n        self.DeviceID = DeviceID\n        self.TimeStamp = TimeStamp\n    }\n\n    public init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {\n        let container = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)\n        DeviceID = try container.decode(String.self, forKey: .DeviceID)\n        // TimeStamp can come as String or number\n        if let tsString = try? container.decode(String.self, forKey: .TimeStamp) {\n            TimeStamp = tsString\n        } else if let tsInt = try? container.decode(Int64.self, forKey: .TimeStamp) {\n            TimeStamp = String(tsInt)\n        } else if let tsDouble = try? container.decode(Double.self, forKey: .TimeStamp) {\n            TimeStamp = String(Int64(tsDouble))\n        } else {\n            TimeStamp = \"0\"\n        }\n    }\n\n    public func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws {\n        var container = encoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)\n        try container.encode(DeviceID, forKey: .DeviceID)\n        try container.encode(TimeStamp, forKey: .TimeStamp)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Server configuration information from GetVisitorHistory response.\npublic struct MiataruVisitorHistoryServerConfig: Codable {\n    public let MaximumNumberOfVisitorHistory: String",

id: localization-strings\n    content: Add all required localization strings to Localizable.xcstrings for all 10 supported languages (en, de, da, es, fi, fr, it, ja, nl, zh-Hans)\n    status: completed\n  - id: mutual-detector\n    content: Create MutualNavigationDetector with polling, hysteresis logic, and visitor history caching\n    status: completed\n  - id: mutual-integration\n    content: Integrate mutual detection into iPhone_DeviceNavigationView - track active navigation and use detector (all text must use NSLocalizedString)\n    status: completed\n  - id: bottom-status-mutual\n    content: Update RouteInfoState and BottomAccessoryModifier to show localized mutual navigation indicator when mutual is active\n    status: completed\n  - Summary of what was wrong and what was changed:

**Cause**  
The `List` had a single child: `VisitorHistoryStateView(...)`. So the list was one big cell (the whole state view), and the `ForEach` lived inside that. In SwiftUI, **swipe actions only work on views that are direct row content of the list**. Because the rows were inside a wrapper view, they were never treated as list rows, so no swipe actions appeared.

**Fix**  
The list was restructured so that the **list’s content is either loading/error/empty or a `ForEach` of rows**:

- The loading, error, and empty states are still shown in the same `List`, but as direct section content.
- When there is data, the `List` now contains a `Section` with a **direct** `ForEach(viewModel.sortedVisitors, ...)`. Each `VisitorHistoryRow` is therefore a direct row of the list, and the same `.swipeActions(edge: .leading, ...)` and `.swipeActions(edge: .trailing, ...)` are applied to each row.

With this structure, leading and trailing swipe actions should show and work on each visitor history row.

Summary of what was wrong and what was changed:

**What was wrong**  
The visitor history you see on the **My Device** tab comes from **VisitorHistorySection**, which is embedded in `iPhone_MyDeviceQRCodeView` (the QR code screen). That section was using a **LazyVStack**, not a **List**. In SwiftUI, **swipe actions only work on rows that are direct content of a List**. So the earlier fix only affected the full-screen Visitor History screen (`iPhone_VisitorHistoryView`), not the list on the My Device tab.

**What was changed**  
**VisitorHistorySection** was updated so the visitor list is backed by a **List** instead of a LazyVStack:

1. **Loading / error / empty**  
   The same loading, error, and empty states are still shown (no List in those cases).

2. **When there are visitors**  
   A **List** is used with a **ForEach** over `viewModel.sortedVisitors`, and the same **leading** and **trailing** `.swipeActions` were added to each row (Add and allow, Ignore / Unignore for unknown visitors).

3. **Embedding in the My Device scroll**  
   - `.listStyle(.plain)` keeps the list visually simple.  
   - `.scrollContentBackground(.hidden)` removes the default list background so it fits the existing scroll layout.  
   - `.scrollDisabled(true)` turns off the List’s own scrolling so the parent **ScrollView** (QR + visitor section) scrolls as one and list rows still get swipe actions.

With this, the visitor list on the **My Device** tab is real List rows, so leading and trailing swipe actions should appear and work there. Try swiping on a visitor row on that tab again.

Summary of the change:

**Cause:** The visitor list is a `List` with `.scrollDisabled(true)` inside the My Device `ScrollView`. With no height set, the list didn’t get a height for all rows, so the scroll view’s content height was too small and you couldn’t scroll down to the last visitors.

- `.frame(minHeight: CGFloat(viewModel.sortedVisitors.count) * 60)`

Each row is 56pt; 60pt per row adds a bit of space for the list separator. The list now has enough height for every row, so the parent `ScrollView` can scroll to the bottom and show all visitor devices.
